contracts/userInterfaces/IMorphoLoanSuba.content:
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
pragma solidity >=0.8.4 <0.9;

import {IComposeReceiverAccountBase} from "./IComposeReceiverAccountBase.sol";
import {ISubaccount} from "./ISubaccount.sol";

/*
 * What each action of the wire schema ({ILoanSubaccount}, where the payload layouts are) does on
 * this market.
 *
 * `ACTION_BORROW`. The account's whole idle FXRP balance - the authenticated bridged amount (the
 * codec's `amountLD`) plus any residue - becomes collateral, and the borrowed loan tokens go to
 * the payload's destination. The fee terms are the type's current terms at delivery (the front
 * end warns while a change is pending in the timelock and keeps deadlines short; see the spec).
 * It is a debt increase: pause-gated and subject to the per-type borrow switch, both of which
 * revert retriably. **The cover gate** applies to the post-borrow position: its collateral (the
 * supplied credit included), at the market oracle's price, must cover `1.155 / LLTV` of the new
 * debt plus twice the collectible fee - the same rule as the withdraw's, Morpho's own liquidation
 * line with a headroom, so it implies Morpho's health check - or the delivery reverts retriably
 * (`InsufficientRemainingCollateral`) with nothing supplied or disbursed. Morpho's check runs
 * first, inside its borrow, so a borrow past Morpho's own line (or under a dead oracle) fails
 * there with Morpho's error instead; and unlike the withdraw, a borrow has no oracle-free route -
 * it needs the oracle back.
 *
 * `ACTION_WITHDRAW`. **The exit gate**: the withdrawal passes while the collateral remaining
 * after it, valued at the market oracle's price, covers `1.155 / LLTV` of the live debt plus
 * twice the collectible fee (1.5x at the launch market's 77% LLTV - Morpho's own liquidation line
 * with a headroom, so the gate implies Morpho's health check), and otherwise reverts retriably
 * (`InsufficientRemainingCollateral`, carrying the required cover and the remaining value) - debt
 * and fee are paid in loan tokens through {repay}, never taken from the collateral, so no price
 * ever moves funds here. Every failure leaves the delivery retriable, and this is the one place
 * what recovers it is written out. A quote shortfall: retry the SAME packet with more value.
 * Another transient return-send failure: retry the same packet once its cause clears - more value
 * cannot help, since exactly the newly quoted fee is forwarded. An uncovered remainder
 * (`InsufficientRemainingCollateral`, which a dead or zero-priced oracle also produces, since
 * it values the remainder at nothing): repay - send loan tokens to the account and let {repay}
 * split them pro rata between debt and fee (every payment shrinks the required cover; covering
 * both settles the position once the fee has actually been collected - a fee the collector
 * cannot receive stays owed and reserved, and a later {repay} retries it) - after which the
 * retried delivery passes, oracle-free once nothing is owed; or sign a smaller withdrawal. Bad
 * `returnOptions` frozen into the signed packet (the accepted residual - no retry can fix the
 * blob itself): issue a corrected instruction reusing the SAME operation id, whereupon the parked
 * packet later duplicate-skips. Position health is enforced by Morpho.
 *
 * `ACTION_DEPOSIT_COLLATERAL`. Supplies the account's whole idle FXRP balance as collateral on
 * its one market: the authenticated bridged amount (the codec's `amountLD`, which must be
 * non-zero) plus any residue waiting for the permissionless rail, less whatever that rail already
 * put into the position before delivery; no debt changes hands. While the controller is paused it
 * executes only when the position carries live debt (the defensive case - protecting an
 * endangered position); a debt-free deposit is new exposure and waits out the pause.
 *
 * `ACTION_CANCEL`. Consumes the id and nothing more: no market read, no fee terms, no borrow
 * switch, no collateral or debt moves. It is not pause-gated, since revoking an authority is not
 * new exposure.
 */

/**
 * @title IMorphoLoanSubaccountRemote
 * @notice User interface for the loan-chain-side subaccount (Ethereum, at launch), at the same
 * CREATE2 address as its Flare counterpart. Authenticated compose payloads, sent by this same
 * account on Flare, execute the typed actions on the type's write-once Morpho market — so the
 * address itself commits to the pool. Repayment, idle-collateral deposit and the fee
 * checkpoint are permissionless fixed rails, and nothing here is parent-callable. Idle FXRP
 * has one route, into the position ({depositIdleFxrp}), from where
 * the signed withdraw action brings it home under the position's ordinary conditions. Across
 * the rails and the signed actions every destination is fixed on-chain - the account's own
 * position, the parent, the governance-set fee recipient, or (the withdraw's return leg) this
 * account's own address on Flare - while the one user-chosen destination is a signed
 * borrow's disbursement. It has no native rail.
 */
interface IMorphoLoanSubaccountRemote is IComposeReceiverAccountBase, ISubaccount {

    /**
     * @notice The position as the front end needs it, projected to the current block: Morpho's
     * debt brought forward the way its accrual will bring it (the market's rate model over the
     * time since the market's last update), the fee's current period priced at the snapshotted
     * terms. Every field is a quote for the observed block - the contract recomputes at delivery.
     * @param collateral Collateral in the Morpho position, in collateral-token base units.
     * @param idleCollateral Collateral on the account, not in the position: the deposit rail, the
     * deposit action or the next borrow supplies it; a withdrawal leaves it where it is, so it is
     * not withdrawable position collateral.
     * @param idleLoanToken Loan tokens on the account: repay fuel, a reserved fee or a retained
     * surplus, all of which the next {repay} consumes.
     * @param debt The live Morpho debt, interest to this block included.
     * @param feeDebtX18 The fee payable now - the running period projected to this block - at
     * WAD precision (base units x 1e18); the whole units, `feeDebtX18 / 1e18`, are the
     * collectible.
     * @param oraclePrice The market oracle's price (1e36 scale); zero when the oracle is dead
     * or answers zero - the gate then values the collateral at nothing.
     * @param collateralValue `collateral` at that price, in loan tokens.
     * @param lltv The market's liquidation LTV (WAD).
     * @param requiredCover The cover gate's demand on the position as it stands, in loan tokens.
     * @param morphoHealthFactor Morpho's distance to liquidation, `collateralValue x lltv / debt`
     * (WAD): above 1e18 healthy, 1e18 on Morpho's line; the maximum value when debt-free; zero
     * when the oracle is dead with live debt. Flare's cover is the stricter line - compare
     * `collateralValue` with `requiredCover` for that one.
     * @param liquidationPrice The lowest oracle price (1e36 scale) at which Morpho still holds
     * the position healthy, both of its floor steps included: one unit below it the position is
     * liquidatable. Zero when debt-free (never liquidatable), the maximum value when there is
     * debt and no collateral (liquidatable at any price).
     */
    struct LoanPosition {
        uint256 collateral;
        uint256 idleCollateral;
        uint256 idleLoanToken;
        uint256 debt;
        uint256 feeDebtX18;
        uint256 oraclePrice;
        uint256 collateralValue;
        uint256 lltv;
        uint256 requiredCover;
        uint256 morphoHealthFactor;
        uint256 liquidationPrice;
    }

    /**
     * @notice What the cover gate and the market allow next, projected to the current block.
     * @param maxBorrowByCover The largest further borrow the cover gate passes once the idle
     * collateral and `additionalCollateral` are supplied with it (Morpho's own rounding
     * included); zero under a dead oracle. The cover check only: the pool's liquidity
     * (`marketLiquidity`), the pause, the borrow switch and the transport are separate
     * conditions.
     * @param marketLiquidity The loan tokens the pool can still lend: its supply total minus its
     * borrow total, both brought to this block. Morpho refuses a borrow above it.
     * @param maxWithdraw The largest withdrawal the cover gate passes on the position as it
     * stands: the whole collateral when nothing is owed, zero under a dead oracle otherwise. The
     * cover check only; the pause and the transport are separate conditions.
     */
    struct LoanLimits {
        uint256 maxBorrowByCover;
        uint256 marketLiquidity;
        uint256 maxWithdraw;
    }

    /**
     * @notice What a {repay} would do now with the loan tokens already on the account plus a
     * top-up - the EXPECTED allocation: a fee transfer the collector's token refuses is deferred
     * or reserved at execution instead, so the fee then stays owed and the debt takes its share.
     * Oracle-free, like {repay} itself. The payment allocated is the loan tokens on the account
     * plus the top-up.
     * @param feePaid The fee collected: the pro-rata share of a payment short of debt plus fee,
     * the whole collectible otherwise.
     * @param debtPaid The Morpho repayment.
     * @param surplus Pushed to the parent - only once the debt is closed; anything else that is
     * left stays on the account (a reserved fee, or the remainder of a partial payment).
     * @param debtAfter The Morpho debt afterwards, Morpho's rounding included.
     * @param collectibleAfter The fee still payable afterwards.
     * @param closingTopUp The top-up that closes both claims now: debt plus collectible, less
     * what is already on the account.
     */
    struct RepayPreview {
        uint256 feePaid;
        uint256 debtPaid;
        uint256 surplus;
        uint256 debtAfter;
        uint256 collectibleAfter;
        uint256 closingTopUp;
    }

    /**
     * @notice Whether a withdrawal of a given amount passes the cover gate now, and what
     * reopens it if not. The cover check only: an amount above the collateral, the pause and the
     * transport are Morpho's and the delivery's own refusals.
     * @param coverSatisfied True when the cover check passes the withdrawal on the position as
     * it stands - the check, not a promise of execution.
     * @param requiredCover The cover the gate demands, in loan tokens.
     * @param remainingValue The collateral left after the withdrawal at the oracle's price;
     * zero under a dead oracle.
     * @param minimumTopUp The smallest loan-token top-up whose {repay}, together with the loan
     * tokens already on the account, makes the withdrawal pass - the expected allocation, see
     * {previewRepay}; zero when it already passes. Closing both claims always suffices.
     */
    struct WithdrawPreview {
        bool coverSatisfied;
        uint256 requiredCover;
        uint256 remainingValue;
        uint256 minimumTopUp;
    }

    /**
     * @notice Whether a borrow of a given amount, with the idle collateral and a packet's
     * collateral supplied first, passes the cover gate now - the cover check only; the pool's
     * liquidity is reported beside it, the pause, the borrow switch and the transport are
     * separate conditions, and the amount is not otherwise validated.
     * @param coverSatisfied True when the post-borrow position passes the cover check.
     * @param requiredCover The cover the gate demands of the post-borrow position, in loan
     * tokens.
     * @param collateralValue The supplied collateral - in the position, idle and the packet's -
     * at the oracle's price; zero under a dead oracle.
     * @param debtAfter The Morpho debt after the borrow, its share rounding included.
     * @param marketLiquidity The loan tokens the pool can still lend; Morpho refuses a borrow
     * above it.
     */
    struct BorrowPreview {
        bool coverSatisfied;
        uint256 requiredCover;
        uint256 collateralValue;
        uint256 debtAfter;
        uint256 marketLiquidity;
    }

    /**
     * @notice Emitted when a borrow action executes.
     * @param parentPersonalAccount The parent Personal Account address.
     * @param operationId The user-chosen operation id, now consumed.
     * @param collateralSupplied FXRP supplied in this execution: the whole idle balance - the
     * bridged credit plus any residue, less whatever the permissionless deposit rail had already
     * put into the position (zero for a message-only borrow with nothing idle).
     * @param borrowAmount Loan-token amount borrowed and disbursed (non-zero).
     * @param destinationKind The destination kind (see the `DESTINATION_KIND_*` constants).
     * @param destination The disbursement destination.
     * @param guid The LayerZero message id the action arrived with.
     */
    event LoanOpened(
        address indexed parentPersonalAccount,
        bytes32 operationId,
        uint256 collateralSupplied,
        uint256 borrowAmount,
        uint8 destinationKind,
        bytes32 destination,
        bytes32 guid
    );

    /**
     * @notice Emitted when a deposit-collateral action executes.
     * @param parentPersonalAccount The parent Personal Account address.
     * @param amount FXRP supplied in this execution: the whole idle balance - the bridged credit
     * plus any residue, less whatever the permissionless deposit rail had already put into the
     * position.
     * @param guid The LayerZero message id the action arrived with.
     */
    event CollateralDeposited(
        address indexed parentPersonalAccount,
        uint256 amount,
        bytes32 guid
    );

    /**
     * @notice Emitted when a withdraw action executes; the withdrawn collateral is bridged
     * home in the same execution ({FXrpBridgedToOrigin} follows).
     * @param parentPersonalAccount The parent Personal Account address.
     * @param operationId The user-chosen operation id, now consumed.
     * @param amount Collateral withdrawn from the position and bridged.
     * @param guid The LayerZero message id the action arrived with.
     */
    event CollateralWithdrawn(
        address indexed parentPersonalAccount,
        bytes32 operationId,
        uint256 amount,
        bytes32 guid
    );

    /**
     * @notice Emitted when a cancel action consumes an operation id, so the borrow or withdraw
     * packet carrying that id can no longer execute. Absent when the id was already consumed -
     * the original won the race, or the cancellation was delivered twice.
     * @param parentPersonalAccount The parent Personal Account address.
     * @param operationId The operation id now consumed.
     * @param guid The LayerZero message id the cancellation arrived with.
     */
    event LoanActionCancelled(
        address indexed parentPersonalAccount,
        bytes32 operationId,
        bytes32 guid
    );

    /**
     * @notice Emitted when idle loan tokens are repaid into the account's position.
     * @param parentPersonalAccount The parent Personal Account address.
     * @param assets The assets repaid (clamped to the live debt).
     */
    event LoanRepaid(
        address indexed parentPersonalAccount,
        uint256 assets
    );

    /**
     * @notice Emitted when idle FXRP is deposited as collateral into the account's position.
     * @param parentPersonalAccount The parent Personal Account address.
     * @param amount The amount deposited.
     */
    event IdleFxrpDeposited(
        address indexed parentPersonalAccount,
        uint256 amount
    );

    /**
     * @notice Emitted when FXRP is bridged back to this account's address on the origin
     * chain, to be redeemed on arrival: a withdraw action's return leg.
     * @param parentPersonalAccount The parent Personal Account address.
     * @param amount The amount bridged.
     * @param originEid The origin chain's LayerZero endpoint id.
     * @param guid The LayerZero message id of the bridge-back send.
     */
    event FXrpBridgedToOrigin(
        address indexed parentPersonalAccount,
        uint256 amount,
        uint32 originEid,
        bytes32 guid
    );

    /**
     * @notice Emitted when native value is forwarded to the parent Personal Account
     * (the remote implementation): the excess of a withdraw action's return-leg fee, or the whole value of a
     * terminally skipped withdraw delivery - it must not strand on an account with no
     * native rail.
     * @param parentPersonalAccount The parent Personal Account address paid.
     * @param amount The native value forwarded.
     */
    event NativeSweptToParent(
        address indexed parentPersonalAccount,
        uint256 amount
    );

    /**
     * @notice Emitted after each fee checkpoint and re-baseline, degenerate ones included
     * (zero principal or a zero elapsed period skip the fee math but still re-baseline).
     * @param parentPersonalAccount The parent Personal Account address.
     * @param principal The canonical Morpho debt measured at the checkpoint (base units); a
     * borrow or repayment in the same call re-syncs it afterward
     * ({LoanFeePrincipalSynced}), and {getLoanFeeState} is authoritative.
     * @param feeDeltaX18 The fee accrued for the interval (base units at WAD precision); zero
     * on degenerate checkpoints.
     */
    event LoanFeeCheckpointed(
        address indexed parentPersonalAccount,
        uint256 principal,
        uint256 feeDeltaX18
    );

    /**
     * @notice Emitted when a borrow or repayment re-syncs the fee base to the canonical
     * post-action debt (the clock and terms snapshot stay).
     * @param parentPersonalAccount The parent Personal Account address.
     * @param principal The canonical Morpho debt after the action (base units) - the base
     * the next period is priced on.
     */
    event LoanFeePrincipalSynced(
        address indexed parentPersonalAccount,
        uint256 principal
    );

    /**
     * @notice Emitted when accrued fee is paid to the fee recipient in loan tokens: from the
     * account's balance in {repay} (the fee's pro-rata share of a partial payment, or, once
     * the debt is closed, as much of the collectible as the balance covers).
     * @param feeRecipient The collector paid.
     * @param amount The amount paid (whole base units; the fee debt shrinks by exactly this).
     */
    event LoanFeeCollected(
        address indexed feeRecipient,
        uint256 amount
    );

    /**
     * @notice Emitted when a sub-unit fee remainder is forgiven at an exit gate: on a
     * debt-free position it can never be
     * transferred (ERC-20 moves whole base units) and never grows again, so a raw-zero gate
     * would park the exit forever over less than one base unit. Never more than a sub-unit
     * remainder: a whole base unit or more stays owed.
     * @param remainderX18 The forgiven remainder (base units at WAD precision, below 1e18).
     */
    event LoanFeeRemainderForgiven(
        uint256 remainderX18
    );

    /**
     * @notice Emitted with the amount of outstanding fee covered by loan tokens retained on
     * the account instead of leaving as surplus; a later {repay} retries from it. A snapshot,
     * not a delta: repeated calls can emit the same amount, and a collection that empties the
     * balance reserves zero (the claim then lives only in the fee debt).
     * @param feeRecipient The collector the reservation is owed to.
     * @param amount The reserved amount (whole base units).
     */
    event LoanFeeReserved(
        address indexed feeRecipient,
        uint256 amount
    );

    /**
     * @notice Emitted when the initial pro-rata attempt of a partial {repay} failed to pay
     * the fee's share - the token refused the recipient (RLUSD can freeze addresses). The share
     * stays in the repayment balance and repays debt; if that closes the debt, the remainder
     * is attempted again and whatever still cannot be paid is reserved on the account
     * ({LoanFeeReserved}). Whatever the call leaves unpaid stays owed; a later {repay}
     * collects it.
     * @param feeRecipient The collector the share was owed to.
     * @param amount The unpaid share (whole base units).
     */
    event LoanFeeDeferred(
        address indexed feeRecipient,
        uint256 amount
    );

    /**
     * @notice Emitted when a closed position's loan-token surplus is sent to the parent
     * Personal Account (the user's own account on this chain) at the end of {repay}.
     * @param parentPersonalAccount The parent Personal Account address paid.
     * @param amount The surplus amount.
     */
    event LoanSurplusRecovered(
        address indexed parentPersonalAccount,
        uint256 amount
    );

    /**
     * @notice Emitted when a closed position's loan-token surplus could not be sent to the
     * parent Personal Account (the token refused the transfer - RLUSD can freeze addresses)
     * and stays on the account. The repayment itself stands; a later {repay} retries the push.
     * @param parentPersonalAccount The parent Personal Account address that refused.
     * @param amount The surplus amount retained.
     */
    event LoanSurplusRetained(
        address indexed parentPersonalAccount,
        uint256 amount
    );

    /**
     * @notice Emitted when an authenticated action completes without executing. The bridged
     * FXRP that arrived with the message stays on the account, recoverable along the fixed
     * rails.
     * @param parentPersonalAccount The parent Personal Account address.
     * @param operationId The payload's operation id. A duplicate was already consumed; an
     * expired skip leaves it unconsumed (the intent can retry under it).
     * @param reason The skip reason (see the `SKIP_REASON_*` constants).
     * @param guid The LayerZero message id the action arrived with.
     */
    event LoanActionSkipped(
        address indexed parentPersonalAccount,
        bytes32 operationId,
        uint8 reason,
        bytes32 guid
    );

    /**
     * @notice Reverts on a debt increase while new borrowing is disabled for this account's
     * subaccount type — the routine way a pool is sunset. Deliberately a revert, not a skip:
     * the condition is temporary-by-policy and a permissionless delivery must not consume
     * the packet.
     */
    error BorrowingDisabled();

    /**
     * @notice Reverts a debt increase before the subaccount type's fee recipient activates
     * its terms: a registered-but-unpriced type cannot take on debt. Retriable - the packet
     * is not consumed by this temporary condition.
     */
    error FeeTermsNotConfigured();

    /**
     * @notice Reverts if there are no idle loan tokens.
     */
    error NothingToRepay();

    /**
     * @notice Reverts if there is no idle FXRP to deposit.
     */
    error NothingToDeposit();

    /**
     * @notice Reverts if the OFT's live peer for the origin chain no longer matches the pinned
     * one; the return leg fails closed instead of bridging toward an unknown remote OApp.
     */
    error WrongOriginPeer();

    /**
     * @notice Reverts if the delivered compose value does not cover the return leg's LayerZero
     * messaging fee.
     * @param required The required fee.
     */
    error InsufficientFundsForBridgeHome(
        uint256 required
    );

    /**
     * @notice Reverts if excess or skipped compose value could not be forwarded to the parent
     * (this account has no native exit); the delivery stays retriable.
     */
    error RefundFailed();

    /**
     * @notice Reverts a withdraw delivered below its signed compose-value floor, so that an
     * underfunded permissionless delivery cannot consume the packet - not even as a terminal
     * skip. Retriable.
     * @param required The signed delivery-value floor.
     */
    error InsufficientDeliveryValue(
        uint256 required
    );

    /**
     * @notice Reverts a withdraw or borrow action that would leave the position uncovered: the
     * collateral remaining after it, at the market oracle's price, would be worth less than
     * `1.155 / LLTV` of the live debt plus twice the collectible fee (a dead or zero-priced
     * oracle values it at nothing). Retriable: repay - loan tokens to the account and {repay} -
     * or sign a smaller withdrawal or borrow, then retry.
     * @param requiredCover The collateral value the gate demands, in loan tokens.
     * @param remainingValue The value the action would have left, in loan tokens; zero under
     * a dead or zero-priced oracle.
     */
    error InsufficientRemainingCollateral(
        uint256 requiredCover,
        uint256 remainingValue
    );

    /**
     * @notice Reverts on a borrow with an unsupported destination kind (the Wormhole-to-XRPL
     * kind is reserved but not implemented).
     * @param destinationKind The unsupported destination kind.
     */
    error UnsupportedDestinationKind(
        uint8 destinationKind
    );

    /**
     * @notice Reverts on a borrow that names a delivery-value floor for a destination kind that
     * spends no compose value on this chain. Every kind V1 supports disburses without spending
     * value, so the floor must be zero; the field is reserved in the frozen payload for a kind
     * that pays for its own onward delivery. The Flare sender refuses the same instruction
     * before any bridge fee is paid.
     */
    error UnexpectedDeliveryValueFloor();

    /**
     * @notice Reverts on a borrow disbursement destination that is not a clean zero-padded
     * EVM address, or is zero or this account.
     */
    error InvalidDestination();

    /**
     * @notice Reverts on an action carrying no amount: a borrow with a zero borrow amount, a
     * deposit with no bridged amount, or a withdraw of zero.
     */
    error ZeroAmount();

    /**
     * @notice Repays the account's debt and the accrued Flare fee with its idle loan-token
     * balance: a payment short of the two is split pro rata between them, a covering one
     * closes the debt, attempts the whole collectible (reserving anything unpaid) and returns
     * the surplus to the parent.
     * @dev Permissionless and pause-exempt throughout: the debt reduction only moves the
     * account's own position toward safety, and the fee legs only move money to Flare's own
     * recipient. It checkpoints before the repayment and re-syncs
     * the canonical debt after (see {checkpointFee}). With live debt `D` and collectible fee
     * `F`, interest accrues, then a balance `P < D + F` pays `P × F / (D + F)` (rounded down)
     * to the fee recipient first and repays Morpho with the rest - by exact borrow shares when
     * that rest covers the debt (no over-repay revert), otherwise by assets; a balance covering
     * `D + F` closes the debt by exact shares and attempts the whole collectible from the
     * remainder. Every fee payment is best-effort, never held by the pause (an overcharge
     * would land on Flare's own recipient and is refundable), never rolling back the
     * repayment ({LoanFeeCollected}; the fee debt shrinks only by the
     * successfully requested transfer, conventional ERC-20 semantics being a
     * market-registration policy): a share that cannot be paid stays in the balance and
     * repays debt ({LoanFeeDeferred}), and once debt-free the remainder is attempted again,
     * with as much of it as the outstanding fee needs reserved here ({LoanFeeReserved}). Only
     * the unreserved balance is pushed to the parent once debt-free ({LoanSurplusRecovered};
     * best-effort, {LoanSurplusRetained} on refusal). Settling both claims through this rail
     * therefore costs the live debt plus the collectible fee, from one balance in one call; a
     * payment that covers the debt but not the fee leaves a pro-rata sliver of both, unless
     * the debt closes for less: a paid share's round-down can leave exactly the debt (possible
     * within roughly `F / D` base units of `D + F`), and a deferred share leaves the full
     * payment available, which may cover it - Morpho then consumes exactly the debt and the
     * tail handles any remainder, with fee still outstanding. The default route pays the fee
     * alongside the debt; repaying Morpho directly, on this account's behalf, pays the debt
     * alone.
     * @return _assets The assets repaid.
     */
    function repay()
        external
        returns (uint256 _assets);

    /**
     * @notice Runs a bare fee checkpoint: prices the elapsed period at the snapshotted
     * terms, adds the result to the fee debt, and re-baselines (principal to the canonical
     * live debt, clock to now, snapshot to the current terms).
     * @dev Permissionless and pause-exempt - notably the liquidated account's relief: an
     * external repayment or liquidation is invisible to the account, so the floor keeps
     * accruing on the stale principal until someone checkpoints, and only prospectively.
     * Under unchanged terms and non-decreasing debt, splitting a period typically increases
     * the total fee and never decreases it by more than one X18 unit (under 1e-18 of a base
     * unit) per checkpoint, so checkpointing cannot be used against the protocol; the
     * advertised promise is that per-checkpoint measurement. Shares-first: zero principal
     * makes no Morpho call, zero live shares settle at zero debt without touching the IRM.
     */
    function checkpointFee()
        external;

    /**
     * @notice Deposits the whole idle FXRP balance as collateral into the account's position.
     * @dev Permissionless with a fixed destination (the account's own position): the retry
     * rail for FXRP that arrived without a successful composed action. It remains available
     * while paused only to defend a position with live debt; a debt-free deposit is new
     * exposure and is pause-gated.
     * @return _amount The amount deposited.
     */
    function depositIdleFxrp()
        external
        returns (uint256 _amount);

    /**
     * @notice Returns the account's fee state, as of the last checkpoint or post-action
     * sync (stored values, not a live projection - run {checkpointFee} first for current
     * numbers).
     * @return _principal The canonical Morpho debt at the last checkpoint or sync (base
     * units).
     * @return _feeDebtX18 The accrued, uncollected fee at WAD precision (base units × 1e18);
     * the fractional part below one base unit is carried, never discarded.
     * @return _collectible The fee payable now: `_feeDebtX18 / 1e18`, whole base units.
     * @return _lastCheckpoint The last checkpoint's timestamp.
     * @return _feeFloor The snapshotted floor the next elapsed period is priced at (WAD).

    /**
     * @notice Emitted when a redeem request is made.
     * @param personalAccount The personal account address.
     * @param vault The vault address.
     * @param shares The number of shares to redeem.
     * @param claimableEpoch The epoch when the claim becomes available.
     * @param year The year of the claimable date.
     * @param month The month of the claimable date.
     * @param day The day of the claimable date.
     */
    event RedeemRequested(
        address indexed personalAccount,
        address indexed vault,
        uint256 shares,
        uint256 claimableEpoch,
        uint256 year,
        uint256 month,
        uint256 day
    );

    /**
     * @notice Emitted when a claim is made for a specific date.
     * @param personalAccount The personal account address.
     * @param vault The vault address.
     * @param year The year of the claim.
     * @param month The month of the claim.
     * @param day The day of the claim.
     * @param shares The number of shares claimed.
     * @param amount The amount claimed.
     */
    event Claimed(
        address indexed personalAccount,
        address indexed vault,
        uint256 year,
        uint256 month,
        uint256 day,
        uint256 shares,
        uint256 amount
    );

    /**
     * @notice Reverts if the payment amount is invalid.
     * @param requiredAmount The required payment amount.
     */
    error InvalidPaymentAmount(
        uint256 requiredAmount
    );

    /**
     * @notice Reverts if the transaction ID is invalid.
     */
    error InvalidTransactionId();

    /**
     * @notice Reverts if the instruction is invalid.
     * @param instructionType The invalid instruction type.
     * @param instructionCommand The invalid instruction command.
     */
    error InvalidInstruction(
        uint256 instructionType,
        uint256 instructionCommand
    );

    /**
     * @notice Reverts if the instruction type is invalid.
     * @param instructionType The invalid instruction type.
     */
    error InvalidInstructionType(
        uint256 instructionType
    );

    /**
     * @notice Reverts if the collateral reservation ID is unknown.
     */
    error UnknownCollateralReservationId();

    /**
     * @notice Reverts if minting is not completed.
     */
    error MintingNotCompleted();

    /**
     * @notice Reverts if the amount is invalid.
     */
    error InvalidAmount();

    /**
     * @notice Reverts if the minter is invalid.
     */
    error InvalidMinter();

    /**
     * @notice Reserve collateral for minting operation.
     * @param _xrplAddress The XRPL address requesting the collateral reservation.
     * @param _paymentReference The payment reference associated with the request.
     * @param _transactionId The unique transaction ID for tracking.
     * @return _collateralReservationId The ID of the collateral reservation.
     */
    function reserveCollateral(
        string calldata _xrplAddress,
        bytes32 _paymentReference,
        bytes32 _transactionId
    )
        external payable
        returns (uint256 _collateralReservationId);

    /**
     * @notice Execute deposit after successful minting for _collateralReservationId.
     * @param _collateralReservationId The ID of the collateral reservation request returned
       by `reserveCollateral` call.
     * @param _proof Proof of XRPL transaction.
     * @param _xrplAddress The XRPL address requesting execution.
     */
    function executeDepositAfterMinting(
        uint256 _collateralReservationId,
        IPayment.Proof calldata _proof,
        string calldata _xrplAddress
    )
        external;

    /**
     * @notice Execute an XRPL instruction for a given XRPL address.
     * @param _proof Proof of XRPL transaction.
     * @param _xrplAddress The XRPL address requesting execution.
     */
    function executeInstruction(
        IPayment.Proof calldata _proof,
        string calldata _xrplAddress
    )
        external payable;

    /**
     * @notice Returns the transaction id for a given collateral reservation id.
     * @param _collateralReservationId The collateral reservation id.
     * @return _transactionId The transaction id associated with the collateral reservation.
     */
    function getTransactionIdForCollateralReservation(
        uint256 _collateralReservationId
    )
        external view
        returns (bytes32 _transactionId);

}

import {IXRPPayment} from ".//IXRPPayment.sol";
import {IXRPPaymentNonexistence} from ".//IXRPPaymentNonexistence.sol";
import {RedemptionRequestInfo} from "./data/RedemptionRequestInfo.sol";


/**
 * Extended redemption interface - supports UBA-based redemption (redeemAmount) and
 * XRP destination tag redemption (redeemWithTag).
 */
interface IRedeemExtended {
    /**
     * Redeemer started the redemption with tag process and provided fassets.
     * The amount of fassets corresponding to valueUBA was burned.
     * Several RedemptionWithTagRequested events are emitted, one for every agent redeemed against.
     * (but multiple tickets for the same agent are combined).
     * The agent's collateral is still locked.
     * Such request can only be confirmed with `confirmXRPRedemptionPayment`.
     */
    event RedemptionWithTagRequested(
        address indexed agentVault,
        address indexed redeemer,
        uint256 indexed requestId,
        string paymentAddress,
        uint256 valueUBA,
        uint256 feeUBA,
        uint256 firstUnderlyingBlock,
        uint256 lastUnderlyingBlock,
        uint256 lastUnderlyingTimestamp,
        bytes32 paymentReference,
        address executor,
        uint256 executorFeeNatWei,
        uint256 destinationTag);

    /**
     * In case there were not enough tickets or more than allowed number would have to be redeemed,
     * only partial redemption is done and the `remainingAmountUBA` of the fassets are returned to
     * the redeemer.
     * Emitted by `redeemWithTag` and `redeemAmount`.
     */
    event RedemptionAmountIncomplete(
        address indexed redeemer,
        uint256 remainingAmountUBA);

    /**
     * Redeem (up to) `_amountUBA` FAssets. Like `redeem`, but accepts an arbitrary amount in UBA
     * instead of whole lots. Like `redeem`, does not require a destination tag.
     * NOTE: in some cases not all sent FAssets can be redeemed (either there are not enough tickets or
     * more than a fixed limit of tickets should be redeemed). In this case only part of the approved assets
     * are burned and redeemed and the redeemer can execute this method again for the remaining amount.
     * In such a case the `RedemptionAmountIncomplete` event will be emitted, indicating remaining amount.
     * Agent receives redemption request id and instructions for underlying payment in
     * RedemptionRequested event and has to pay `value - fee` and use the provided payment reference.
     * @param _amountUBA amount of redeemer's FAssets that will be burned; this is NOT the amount of assets
     *      that will be received by the redeemer - the redemption fee will be subtracted
     * @param _redeemerUnderlyingAddressString the address to which the agent must transfer underlying amount
     * @param _executor the account that is allowed to execute redemption default (besides redeemer and agent)
     * @return _redeemedAmountUBA the actual redeemed amount; may be less than requested if there are not enough
     *      redemption tickets available or the maximum redemption ticket limit is reached
     */
    function redeemAmount(
        uint256 _amountUBA,
        string memory _redeemerUnderlyingAddressString,
        address payable _executor
    ) external payable
        returns (uint256 _redeemedAmountUBA);

    /**
     * Redeem (up to) `_amountUBA` f-assets. The corresponding amount of the f-assets belonging
     * to the redeemer will be burned and the redeemer will get paid by the agent in underlying currency
     * (or, in case of agent's payment default, by agent's collateral with a premium).
     * NOTE: in some cases not all sent f-assets can be redeemed (either there are not enough tickets or
     * more than a fixed limit of tickets should be redeemed). In this case only part of the approved assets
     * are burned and redeemed and the redeemer can execute this method again for the remaining amount.
     * In such a case the `RedemptionAmountIncomplete` event will be emitted, indicating the remaining amount.
     * Agent receives redemption request id and instructions for underlying payment in
     * RedemptionRequested event and has to pay `value - fee` and use the provided payment reference.
     * NOTE: if the underlying block isn't updated regularly, it can happen that there is no time for underlying
     * payment. Since the agents cannot know when the next redemption will happen, they should regularly update the
     * underlying time by obtaining fresh proof of latest underlying block and calling `updateCurrentBlock`.
     * @param _amountUBA amount of redeemer's FAssets that will be burned; this is NOT the amount of assets
     *      that will be received by the redeemer - the redemption fee will be subtracted
     * @param _redeemerUnderlyingAddressString the address to which the agent must transfer underlying amount
     * @param _executor the account that is allowed to execute redemption default (besides redeemer and agent)
     * @param _destinationTag the destination tag that is required in the redemption payment (only for XRP;
     *      it must fit in 32 bits for now)
     * @return _redeemedAmountUBA the actual redeemed amount; may be less than requested if there are not enough
     *      redemption tickets available or the maximum redemption ticket limit is reached
     */
    function redeemWithTag(
        uint256 _amountUBA,
        string memory _redeemerUnderlyingAddressString,
        address payable _executor,
        uint256 _destinationTag
    ) external payable
        returns (uint256 _redeemedAmountUBA);

    /**
     * After paying to the redeemer, the agent must call this method to unlock the collateral
     * and to make sure that the redeemer cannot demand payment in collateral on timeout.
     * The same method must be called for any payment status (SUCCESS, FAILED, BLOCKED).
     * In case of FAILED, it just releases agent's underlying funds and the redeemer gets paid in collateral
     * after calling redemptionPaymentDefault.
     * In case of SUCCESS or BLOCKED, remaining underlying funds and collateral are released to the agent.
     * If the agent doesn't confirm payment in enough time (several hours, setting confirmationByOthersAfterSeconds),
     * anybody can do it and get rewarded from agent's vault.
     * NOTE: the only difference between this method and `confirmRedemptionPayment` is that this one accepts
     *   IXRPPayment proof type and supports destination tags.
     * NOTE: may only be called by the owner of the agent vault in the redemption request
     *   except if enough time has passed without confirmation - then it can be called by anybody
     * @param _payment proof of the underlying payment (must contain exact `value - fee` amount and correct
     *      payment reference)
     * @param _redemptionRequestId id of an existing redemption request
     */
    function confirmXRPRedemptionPayment(
        IXRPPayment.Proof calldata _payment,
        uint256 _redemptionRequestId
    ) external;

    /**
     * If the agent doesn't transfer the redeemed underlying assets in time (until the last allowed block on
     * the underlying chain), the redeemer calls this method and receives payment in collateral (with some extra).
     * The agent can also call default if the redeemer is unresponsive, to payout the redeemer and free the
     * remaining collateral.
     * NOTE: the only difference between this method and `redemptionPaymentDefault` is that this one accepts
     *   IXRPPayment proof type and supports destination tags.
     * NOTE: may only be called by the redeemer (= creator of the redemption request),
     *   the executor appointed by the redeemer,
     *   or the agent owner (= owner of the agent vault in the redemption request)
     * @param _proof proof that the agent didn't pay with correct payment reference on the underlying chain
     * @param _redemptionRequestId id of an existing redemption request
     */
    function xrpRedemptionPaymentDefault(
        IXRPPaymentNonexistence.Proof calldata _proof,
        uint256 _redemptionRequestId
    ) external;

    /**
     * If false, calling `redeemWithTag` will revert.
     * For now, only XRP chain supports destination tags, so this flag will be true only on XRP network.
     */
    function redeemWithTagSupported()
        external view
        returns (bool);

    /**
     * Returns the data about an ongoing redemption request.
     * Note: once the redemptions is confirmed, the request is deleted and this method fails.
     * However, if there is no payment and the redemption defaults, the method works and returns status DEFAULTED.
     * Note: this method adds redemptionWithTag specific fields to the data returned by `redemptionRequestInfo`.
     * @param _redemptionRequestId the redemption request id, as used for confirming or defaulting the redemption
     */
    function redemptionRequestInfoExt(uint256 _redemptionRequestId)
        external view
        returns (RedemptionRequestInfo.DataExt memory);
}

import { RandomNumberV2Interface } from "./RandomNumberV2Interface.sol";

/**
 * Relay interface.
 */
interface IRelay is RandomNumberV2Interface {

    struct FeeConfig {
        uint8 protocolId;   // Protocol id for which the fee is set
        uint256 feeInWei;   // Fee in wei
    }

    struct RelayInitialConfig {
        uint32 initialRewardEpochId;                           // The initial reward epoch id.
        uint32 startingVotingRoundIdForInitialRewardEpochId;   // The starting voting round id for the initial
                                                               // reward epoch.
        bytes32 initialSigningPolicyHash;                      // The initial signing policy hash.
        uint8 randomNumberProtocolId;                          // The protocol id of the random number protocol.
        uint32 firstVotingRoundStartTs;                        // The timestamp of the first voting round start.
        uint8 votingEpochDurationSeconds;                      // The duration of a voting epoch in seconds.
        uint32 firstRewardEpochStartVotingRoundId;             // The start voting round id of the first reward epoch.
        uint16 rewardEpochDurationInVotingEpochs;              // The duration of a reward epoch in voting epochs.
        uint16 thresholdIncreaseBIPS;                          // The threshold increase in BIPS for signing with
                                                               // old signing policy.
        uint32 messageFinalizationWindowInRewardEpochs;        // The window of reward epochs for finalizing
                                                               // the protocol messages.
        address payable feeCollectionAddress;                  // Fee collection address
        FeeConfig[] feeConfigs;                                // Fee configurations
    }

    struct RelayGovernanceConfig {
        bytes32 descriptionHash;        // Description hash (should be keccak256("RelayGovernance")
        uint256 chainId;                // Chain id on which is the relay is deployed
        FeeConfig[] newFeeConfigs;      // Fee configurations
    }

    // Event is emitted when a new signing policy is initialized by the signing policy setter.
    event SigningPolicyInitialized(
        uint24 indexed rewardEpochId,   // Reward epoch id
        uint32 startVotingRoundId,      // First voting round id of validity.
                                        // Usually it is the first voting round of reward epoch rewardEpochId.
                                        // It can be later,
                                        // if the confirmation of the signing policy on Flare blockchain gets delayed.
        uint16 threshold,               // Confirmation threshold (absolute value of noramalised weights).
        uint256 seed,                   // Random seed.
        address[] voters,               // The list of eligible voters in the canonical order.
        uint16[] weights,               // The corresponding list of normalised signing weights of eligible voters.
                                        // Normalisation is done by compressing the weights from 32-byte values to
                                        // 2 bytes, while approximately keeping the weight relations.
        bytes signingPolicyBytes,       // The full signing policy byte encoded.
        uint64 timestamp                // Timestamp when this happened
    );

    // Event is emitted when a signing policy is relayed.
    // It contains minimalistic data in order to save gas. Data about the signing policy are
    // extractable from the calldata, assuming prefered usage of direct top-level call to relay().
    event SigningPolicyRelayed(
        uint256 indexed rewardEpochId        // Reward epoch id
    );

    // Event is emitted when a protocol message is relayed.
    event ProtocolMessageRelayed(
        uint8 indexed protocolId,           // Protocol id
        uint32 indexed votingRoundId,       // Voting round id
        bool isSecureRandom,                // Secure random flag
        bytes32 merkleRoot                  // Merkle root of the protocol message
    );

    /**
     * Checks the relay message for sufficient weight of signatures for the _messageHash
     * signed for protocol message Merkle root of the form (1, 0, 0, _messageHash).
     * If the check is successful, reward epoch id of the signing policy is returned.
     * Otherwise the function reverts.
     * @param _relayMessage The relay message.
     * @param _messageHash The hash of the message.
     * @return _rewardEpochId The reward epoch id of the signing policy.
     */
    function verifyCustomSignature(
        bytes calldata _relayMessage,
        bytes32 _messageHash
    )
        external
        returns (uint256 _rewardEpochId);

    /**
     * Checks the relay message for sufficient weight of signatures of the hash of the _config data.
     * If the check is successful, the relay contract is configured with the new _config data, which
     * in particular means that fee configurations are updated.
     * Otherwise the function reverts.
     * @param _relayMessage The relay message.
     * @param _config The new relay configuration.
     */
    function governanceFeeSetup(bytes calldata _relayMessage, RelayGovernanceConfig calldata _config) external;

    /**
     * Finalization function for new signing policies and protocol messages.
     * It can be used as finalization contract on Flare chain or as relay contract on other EVM chain.
     * Can be called in two modes. It expects calldata that is parsed in a custom manner.
     * Hence the transaction calls should assemble relevant calldata in the 'data' field.
     * Depending on the data provided, the contract operations in essentially two modes:
     * (1) Relaying signing policy. The structure of the calldata is:
     *        function signature (4 bytes) + active signing policy
     *             + 0 (1 byte) + new signing policy,
     *     total of exactly 4423 bytes.
     * (2) Relaying signed message. The structure of the calldata is:
     *        function signature (4 bytes) + signing policy
     *           + signed message (38 bytes) + ECDSA signatures with indices (67 bytes each)
     *     This case splits into two subcases:
     *     - protocolMessageId = 1: Message id must be of the form (protocolMessageId, 0, 0, merkleRoot).
     *       The validity of the signatures of sufficient weight is checked and if
     *       successful, the merkleRoot from the message is returned (32 bytes) and the
     *       reward epoch id of the signing policy as well (additional 3 bytes)
     *     - protocolMessageId > 1: The validity of the signatures of sufficient weight is checked and if
     *       it is valid, the merkleRoot is published for protocolId and votingRoundId.
     * Reverts if relaying is not successful.
     */
    function relay() external returns (bytes memory);

    /**
     * Verifies the leaf (or intermediate node) with the Merkle proof against the Merkle root
     * for given protocol id and voting round id.
     * A fee may need to be paid. It is protocol specific.
     * **NOTE:** Overpayment is not refunded.
     * @param _protocolId The protocol id.
     * @param _votingRoundId The voting round id.
     * @param _leaf The leaf (or intermediate node) to verify.
     * @param _proof The Merkle proof.
     * @return True if the verification is successful.
     */
    function verify(uint256 _protocolId, uint256 _votingRoundId, bytes32 _leaf, bytes32[] calldata _proof)
        external payable
        returns (bool);

    /**
     * Returns the address of the signing policy setter.
     * If the address is zero, the contract is used as a pure relay,
     * otherwise the contract is deployed on mainnet.
     */
    function signingPolicySetter() external view returns (address);

    /**
     * Returns the signing policy hash for given reward epoch id.
     * The function is reverted if signingPolicySetter is NOT set, hence on all
     * deployments where the contract is used as a pure relay.
     * @param _rewardEpochId The reward epoch id.
     * @return _signingPolicyHash The signing policy hash.
     */
    function toSigningPolicyHash(uint256 _rewardEpochId) external view returns (bytes32 _signingPolicyHash);

    /**
     * Returns true if there is finalization for a given protocol id and voting round id.
     * @param _protocolId The protocol id.
     * @param _votingRoundId The voting round id.
     */
    function isFinalized(uint256 _protocolId, uint256 _votingRoundId) external view returns (bool);

    /**
     * Returns the Merkle root for given protocol id and voting round id.
     * The function is reverted if signingPolicySetter is NOT set, hence on all
     * deployments where the contract is used as a pure relay.
     * @param _protocolId The protocol id.
     * @param _votingRoundId The voting round id.
     * @return _merkleRoot The Merkle root.
     */
    function merkleRoots(uint256 _protocolId, uint256 _votingRoundId) external view returns (bytes32 _merkleRoot);

    /**
     * Returns the start voting round id for given reward epoch id.
     * @param _rewardEpochId The reward epoch id.
     * @return _startingVotingRoundId The start voting round id.
     */
    function startingVotingRoundIds(uint256 _rewardEpochId) external view returns (uint256 _startingVotingRoundId);

    /**
     * Returns the voting round id for given timestamp.
     * @param _timestamp The timestamp.
     * @return _votingRoundId The voting round id.
     */
    function getVotingRoundId(uint256 _timestamp) external view returns (uint256 _votingRoundId);

    /**
     * Returns last initialized reward epoch data.
     * @return _lastInitializedRewardEpoch Last initialized reward epoch.
     * @return _startingVotingRoundIdForLastInitializedRewardEpoch Starting voting round id for it.
     */
    function lastInitializedRewardEpochData()
        external view
        returns (
            uint32 _lastInitializedRewardEpoch,
            uint32 _startingVotingRoundIdForLastInitializedRewardEpoch
        );

    /**
     * Returns fee collection address.
     */
    function feeCollectionAddress() external view returns (address payable);

    /**
     * Returns fee in wei for one verification of a given protocol id.
     * @param _protocolId The protocol id.
     */
    function protocolFeeInWei(uint256 _protocolId) external view returns (uint256);

    /**
     * Returns the state data.
     * @return randomNumberProtocolId The protocol id of the random number protocol.
     * @return firstVotingRoundStartTs The timestamp of the first voting round start.
     * @return votingEpochDurationSeconds The duration of a voting epoch in seconds.
     * @return firstRewardEpochStartVotingRoundId The start voting round id of the first reward epoch.
     * @return rewardEpochDurationInVotingEpochs The duration of a reward epoch in voting epochs.
     * @return thresholdIncreaseBIPS The threshold increase in BIPS for signing with old signing policy.
     * @return randomVotingRoundId The random voting round id.
     * @return isSecureRandom The secure random flag.
     * @return lastInitializedRewardEpoch The last initialized reward epoch.
     * @return noSigningPolicyRelay The flag indicating no signing policy relay.
     * @return messageFinalizationWindowInRewardEpochs The window of reward epochs for finalizing the
     *  protocol messages.
     */
    function stateData()
        external
        view
        returns (
            uint8 randomNumberProtocolId,
            uint32 firstVotingRoundStartTs,
            uint8 votingEpochDurationSeconds,
            uint32 firstRewardEpochStartVotingRoundId,
            uint16 rewardEpochDurationInVotingEpochs,
            uint16 thresholdIncreaseBIPS,
            uint32 randomVotingRoundId,
            bool isSecureRandom,
            uint32 lastInitializedRewardEpoch,
            bool noSigningPolicyRelay,
            uint32 messageFinalizationWindowInRewardEpochs
        );

}

interface IVPToken is IERC20 {

     * @notice Delegate by percentage `_bips` of voting power to `_to` from `msg.sender`.
     * @param _to The address of the recipient
     * @param _bips The percentage of voting power to be delegated expressed in basis points (1/100 of one percent).
     *   Not cumulative - every call resets the delegation value (and value of 0 undelegates `to`).
     **/
    function delegate(address _to, uint256 _bips) external;
    
    /**
     * @notice Undelegate all percentage delegations from the sender and then delegate corresponding 
     *   `_bips` percentage of voting power from the sender to each member of `_delegatees`.
     * @param _delegatees The addresses of the new recipients.
     * @param _bips The percentages of voting power to be delegated expressed in basis points (1/100 of one percent).
     *   Total of all `_bips` values must be at most 10000.
     **/
    function batchDelegate(address[] memory _delegatees, uint256[] memory _bips) external;
        
    /**
     * @notice Explicitly delegate `_amount` of voting power to `_to` from `msg.sender`.
     * @param _to The address of the recipient
     * @param _amount An explicit vote power amount to be delegated.

     **/    
    function delegateExplicit(address _to, uint _amount) external;

    /**
    * @notice Revoke all delegation from sender to `_who` at given block. 
    *    Only affects the reads via `votePowerOfAtCached()` in the block `_blockNumber`.
    *    Block `_blockNumber` must be in the past. 
    *    This method should be used only to prevent rogue delegate voting in the current voting block.
    *    To stop delegating use delegate/delegateExplicit with value of 0 or undelegateAll/undelegateAllExplicit.
    * @param _who Address of the delegatee
    * @param _blockNumber The block number at which to revoke delegation.
    */
    function revokeDelegationAt(address _who, uint _blockNumber) external;
    
    /**
     * @notice Undelegate all voting power for delegates of `msg.sender`
     *    Can only be used with percentage delegation.
     *    Does not reset delegation mode back to NOTSET.
     **/
    function undelegateAll() external;
    
    /**
     * @notice Undelegate all explicit vote power by amount delegates for `msg.sender`.
     *    Can only be used with explicit delegation.
     *    Does not reset delegation mode back to NOTSET.
     * @param _delegateAddresses Explicit delegation does not store delegatees' addresses, 
     *   so the caller must supply them.
     * @return The amount still delegated (in case the list of delegates was incomplete).
     */
    function undelegateAllExplicit(address[] memory _delegateAddresses) external returns (uint256);


    /**
     * @dev Should be compatible with ERC20 method
     */
    function name() external view returns (string memory);

    /**
     * @dev Should be compatible with ERC20 method
     */
    function symbol() external view returns (string memory);

    /**
     * @dev Should be compatible with ERC20 method
     */
    function decimals() external view returns (uint8);

     * @param _blockNumber The block number when the totalSupply is queried
     * @return The total amount of tokens at `_blockNumber`
     **/
    function totalSupplyAt(uint _blockNumber) external view returns(uint256);

    /**
     * @dev Queries the token balance of `_owner` at a specific `_blockNumber`.
     * @param _owner The address from which the balance will be retrieved.

     **/
    function balanceOfAt(address _owner, uint _blockNumber) external view returns (uint256);

    
    /**
     * @notice Get the current total vote power.
     * @return The current total vote power (sum of all accounts' vote powers).
     */
    function totalVotePower() external view returns(uint256);
    
    /**
    * @notice Get the total vote power at block `_blockNumber`
    * @param _blockNumber The block number at which to fetch.
    * @return The total vote power at the block  (sum of all accounts' vote powers).
    */
    function totalVotePowerAt(uint _blockNumber) external view returns(uint256);

     * @param _owner The address to get voting power.

     */
    function votePowerOf(address _owner) external view returns(uint256);
    
    /**
    * @notice Get the vote power of `_owner` at block `_blockNumber`
    * @param _owner The address to get voting power.
    * @param _blockNumber The block number at which to fetch.
    * @return Vote power of `_owner` at `_blockNumber`.
    */
    function votePowerOfAt(address _owner, uint256 _blockNumber) external view returns(uint256);

    /**
    * @notice Get the vote power of `_owner` at block `_blockNumber`, ignoring revocation information (and cache).
    * @param _owner The address to get voting power.
    * @param _blockNumber The block number at which to fetch.
    * @return Vote power of `_owner` at `_blockNumber`. Result doesn't change if vote power is revoked.
    */
    function votePowerOfAtIgnoringRevocation(address _owner, uint256 _blockNumber) external view returns(uint256);

    /**
     * @notice Get the delegation mode for '_who'. This mode determines whether vote power is
     *  allocated by percentage or by explicit value. Once the delegation mode is set, 
     *  it never changes, even if all delegations are removed.
     * @param _who The address to get delegation mode.
     * @return delegation mode: 0 = NOTSET, 1 = PERCENTAGE, 2 = AMOUNT (i.e. explicit)
     */
    function delegationModeOf(address _who) external view returns(uint256);
        
    /**
    * @notice Get current delegated vote power `_from` delegator delegated `_to` delegatee.
    * @param _from Address of delegator
    * @param _to Address of delegatee
    * @return The delegated vote power.
    */
    function votePowerFromTo(address _from, address _to) external view returns(uint256);
    
    /**
    * @notice Get delegated the vote power `_from` delegator delegated `_to` delegatee at `_blockNumber`.
    * @param _from Address of delegator
    * @param _to Address of delegatee
    * @param _blockNumber The block number at which to fetch.
    * @return The delegated vote power.
    */
    function votePowerFromToAt(address _from, address _to, uint _blockNumber) external view returns(uint256);
    
    /**
     * @notice Compute the current undelegated vote power of `_owner`
     * @param _owner The address to get undelegated voting power.
     * @return The unallocated vote power of `_owner`
     */
    function undelegatedVotePowerOf(address _owner) external view returns(uint256);
    
    /**
     * @notice Get the undelegated vote power of `_owner` at given block.
     * @param _owner The address to get undelegated voting power.
     * @param _blockNumber The block number at which to fetch.
     * @return The undelegated vote power of `_owner` (= owner's own balance minus all delegations from owner)
     */
    function undelegatedVotePowerOfAt(address _owner, uint256 _blockNumber) external view returns(uint256);
    
    /**
    * @notice Get the vote power delegation `delegationAddresses` 
    *  and `_bips` of `_who`. Returned in two separate positional arrays.
    * @param _who The address to get delegations.
    * @return _delegateAddresses Positional array of delegation addresses.
    * @return _bips Positional array of delegation percents specified in basis points (1/100 or 1 percent)
    * @return _count The number of delegates.
    * @return _delegationMode The mode of the delegation (NOTSET=0, PERCENTAGE=1, AMOUNT=2).
    */
    function delegatesOf(address _who)
        external view 
        returns (
            address[] memory _delegateAddresses,
            uint256[] memory _bips,
            uint256 _count, 
            uint256 _delegationMode
        );
        
    /**
    * @notice Get the vote power delegation `delegationAddresses` 
    *  and `pcts` of `_who`. Returned in two separate positional arrays.
    * @param _who The address to get delegations.
    * @param _blockNumber The block for which we want to know the delegations.
    * @return _delegateAddresses Positional array of delegation addresses.
    * @return _bips Positional array of delegation percents specified in basis points (1/100 or 1 percent)
    * @return _count The number of delegates.
    * @return _delegationMode The mode of the delegation (NOTSET=0, PERCENTAGE=1, AMOUNT=2).
    */
    function delegatesOfAt(address _who, uint256 _blockNumber)
        external view 
        returns (
            address[] memory _delegateAddresses, 
            uint256[] memory _bips, 
            uint256 _count, 
            uint256 _delegationMode
        );

    /**
     * Returns VPContract used for readonly operations (view methods).
     * The only non-view method that might be called on it is `revokeDelegationAt`.
     *
     * @notice `readVotePowerContract` is almost always equal to `writeVotePowerContract`
     * except during upgrade from one VPContract to a new version (which should happen
     * rarely or never and will be anounced before).
     *
     * @notice You shouldn't call any methods on VPContract directly, all are exposed
     * via VPToken (and state changing methods are forbidden from direct calls). 
     * This is the reason why this method returns `IVPContractEvents` - it should only be used
     * for listening to events (`Revoke` only).
     */
    function readVotePowerContract() external view returns (IVPContractEvents);

    /**
     * Returns VPContract used for state changing operations (non-view methods).
     * The only non-view method that might be called on it is `revokeDelegationAt`.
     *
     * @notice `writeVotePowerContract` is almost always equal to `readVotePowerContract`
     * except during upgrade from one VPContract to a new version (which should happen
     * rarely or never and will be anounced before). In the case of upgrade,
     * `writeVotePowerContract` will be replaced first to establish delegations, and
     * after some perio (e.g. after a reward epoch ends) `readVotePowerContract` will be set equal to it.
     *
     * @notice You shouldn't call any methods on VPContract directly, all are exposed
     * via VPToken (and state changing methods are forbidden from direct calls). 
     * This is the reason why this method returns `IVPContractEvents` - it should only be used
     * for listening to events (`Delegate` and `Revoke` only).
     */
    function writeVotePowerContract() external view returns (IVPContractEvents);
    
    /**
     * When set, allows token owners to participate in governance voting
     * and delegate governance vote power.
     */
    function governanceVotePower() external view returns (IGovernanceVotePower);
}

MorphoMath.metadata: {"compiler":{"version":"0.8.35+commit.47b9dedd"},"language":"Solidity","output":{"abi":[],"devdoc":{"kind":"dev","methods":{},"title":"MorphoMath","version":1},"userdoc":{"kind":"user","methods":{},"notice":"Our own MIT implementation of the pieces of Morpho Blue arithmetic the accounts depend on: the market id (`keccak256(abi.encode(marketParams))`, Morpho's `MarketParamsLib.id`), the share/asset conversions with Morpho's virtual offsets (`SharesMathLib`: one virtual asset, 1e6 virtual shares, rounding as named) and the interest compounding of its accrual (`MathLib.wTaylorCompounded`, the third-order Taylor polynomial of `e^(rate * elapsed) - 1` that `_accrueInterest` applies to the borrow total). If the transaction cannot be fetched or the transaction is in a block that does not have a sufficient number of confirmations, the attestation request is rejected. Once the transaction is received, the response fields are extracted if the transaction is balance decreasing for the indicated address. Some of the request and response fields are chain specific as described below. The fields can be computed with the help of a balance decreasing summary. ### UTXO (Bitcoin and Dogecoin) - `sourceAddressIndicator` is the the index of the transaction input in hex padded to a 0x prefixed 32-byte string. If the indicated input does not exist or the indicated input does not have the address, the attestation request is rejected. The `sourceAddress` is the address of the indicated transaction input. - `spentAmount` is the sum of values of all inputs with sourceAddress minus the sum of all outputs with `sourceAddress`. Can be negative. - `blockTimestamp` is the mediantime of a block. ### XRPL - `sourceAddressIndicator` is the standard address hash of the address whose balance has been decreased. If the address indicated by `sourceAddressIndicator` is not among the signers of the transaction and the balance of the address was not lowered in the transaction, the attestation request is rejected. - `spentAmount` is the difference between the balance of the indicated address after and before the transaction. Can be negative. - `blockTimestamp` is the close_time of a ledger converted to unix time.","kind":"dev","methods":{},"version":1},"userdoc":{"kind":"user","methods":{},"notice":"A detection of a transaction that either decreases the balance for some address or is signed by the source address. Such an attestation could prove a violation of an agreement and therefore provides grounds to liquidate some funds locked by a smart contract on Flare. A transaction is considered \u201cbalance decreasing\u201d for the address, if the balance after the transaction is lower than before or the address is among the signers of the transaction (even if The search range are blocks between heights including `minimalBlockNumber` and excluding `firstOverflowBlockNumber`. If the verifier does not have a view of all blocks from `minimalBlockNumber` to `firstOverflowBlockNumber`,  the attestation request is rejected. The request is confirmed if no transaction meeting the specified criteria is found in the search range. Criteria for the transaction: - The transaction is of type payment. - The destination address hash matches the hash of the destination address of the transaction. - If `checkFirstMemoData` is true, the hash of the MemoData field of the first Memo in the transaction matches `firstMemoDataHash`. - If `checkDestinationTag` is true, the destination tag of the transaction matches `destinationTag`. At least one of the fields `checkFirstMemoData` and `checkDestinationTag` must be true for the request to be valid. - One of the following is true:   - Transaction status is `SUCCESS` and the amount received by the specified destination address is greater  than the specified `value`.   - Transaction status is `RECEIVER_FAILURE` and the specified destination address would receive an amount greater than the specified `value` had the transaction been successful. @dev Shared forward-move core of the type's instructions: bridges exactly `_amount` FXRP
 over LayerZero to this account's own address on its type's remote chain, so every entry
 point shares the same guards by construction. A zero amount is a message-only send that
 skips the FAssets-registry lookup, the balance read and the approval (the adapter still
 runs a zero-value pull on the token); the destination is never caller-chosen.
 Exactly the quoted fee is spent; the caller's excess is returned.

@dev The redeem-home compose carries the executor fee as compose value and spends it in
 the same call; no other action here may carry value.

@dev Before expiry, redeems at most the authenticated `_amountLD` (the cap limits the
 amount, not the token provenance - FXRP is fungible) with the compose value as the
 executor fee, zero included. After the sender-stamped deadline the packet skips
 terminally: the balance is left for {sweepRedeem} and the value goes to the parent, so a
 packet cannot outlive its delivery window as a standing instruction over later funds.

@dev Shared redemption core: the public rail uses the whole balance, a compose delivery
 caps it at the authenticated `amountLD`. The parent redeems the amount with `_fee` as
 the executor fee, or receives it unredeemed below the FAssets minimum, and receives all
 attached value - never `msg.sender`, which on the compose path is the endpoint.

@title ComposeReceiverAccountBase contract
 @notice Shared authenticated `lzCompose` ingress and operation-id replay protection for the
 accounts that receive compose messages from their own twin on the other chain. Derived
 accounts define their action set ({_dispatch}), their transport source ({_getTransport}),
 whether compose value is accepted ({_acceptsComposeValue}) and their identity; their
 parent-driven and public rails stay outside this base. The authentication is deliberately in
 one place: it is the security root of every action that arrives without a local signature.
 @dev STORAGE: the consumed operation ids live in the
 `smartAccounts.ComposeReceiverAccountBase.State` namespace (see the storage rule on
 {ControlledAccountBase}), so this base can grow without shifting any lineage that
 inherits it.

 @notice The Flare implementation of the loan subaccount type: the parent-driven loan
 instructions - {borrow}, {depositCollateral} and {withdraw} - each a typed payload the
 loan-chain twin executes on arrival, built here so a malformed payload cannot reach the
 bridge, and sent through the shared forward move of {BridgingSubaccountBase} (the type's
 route, the live peer re-check, the exact quoted fee). Everything else the account does on
 Flare - the permissionless `sweepRedeem`, redeeming its twin's bridge-back on arrival - is
 the bridging surface every such type shares, in the base.
 @dev The controller (MasterAccountController Diamond) is the beacon: the proxy and this
 implementation resolve through `implementationForType`. No `receive()` and no native exit -

@dev The subaccount's action set (see {ComposeReceiverAccountBase._dispatch}).

@dev The withdraw action spends compose value in the same call - the return leg's
 LayerZero fee, with the excess pushed to the parent - so it opts in; every
 other action must not carry value (a mistaken delivery stays retriable without it).
 @dev Adding `ACTION_BORROW` here is what enables a destination kind that pays for its own
 onward delivery, and it must account for the native in three places, not one: a
 SUCCESSFUL EVM disbursement would then be allowed to carry value it never spends (this
 path leaves native untouched, and the account has no rail to recover it, so that value
 must be refused or refunded), a terminal skip already sweeps to the parent, and whatever
 the onward delivery leaves unspent must go the same way.

@dev Consumes an operation id so the borrow or withdraw packet carrying it can never
 execute. Deliberately minimal: no pause check (revoking an authority is not new
 exposure), no deadline (a late cancellation is unnecessary or still correct), no market
 or terms read, nothing moved. An id already consumed - the original executed first, or
 this cancellation was delivered twice - finalizes without an event rather than
 reverting, so a lost race cannot leave the packet retriable forever.

typeDescriptions.typeString: function (uint256) view external returns (struct IMorphoLoanMarketsFacet.FeeTerms memory)

documentation.text:
@dev Supplies the whole idle FXRP balance as collateral - the authenticated bridged
 amount and any residue - without changing debt. The action carries no operation id and
 no deadline: a deposit only adds the user's own collateral, which the permissionless
 rail can do with the same tokens anyway, so a re-issued one (a new packet - a delivered
 compose cannot replay) deposits again and a late one
 is harmless (the same reasoning that leaves the Flare redeem-home id-less). During a
 pause only an indebted position may receive it - defending stays available, new
 exposure waits - and a temporary rejection reverts, leaving the packet retriable.

@dev Supplies the account's whole FXRP balance as collateral and returns the amount, zero
 when nothing is here. Every FXRP on this account is the user's own and has one route, the
 position: a packet's freshly delivered credit, a skipped packet's credit, a direct send -
 there is no distinction to draw, so all of it goes in. The permissionless rail may have
 put a credit into the position before its packet is delivered (the accepted race),
 leaving nothing to supply; a message-only borrow arrives with nothing idle by design.

@dev Borrows `_amount` on the position as it stands and sends it to the destination.
 The fee is checkpointed before and its principal re-synced after (an unsynced new
 principal would read as market interest at the next checkpoint), and the cover gate runs
 on the resulting position before anything leaves: a borrow past it reverts, retriably,
 with nothing sent. Morpho's own health check ran inside the borrow; the gate implies
 it, so it is the binding one whenever Morpho passed.

@dev The atomic withdrawal: withdraws collateral and bridges the withdrawn amount home
 with the redeem-home compose in the same execution - no idle window, so the redeposit race
 cannot touch a withdrawal. The delivered compose value pays the return leg's live quote
 against the signed `returnOptions`, with the excess to the parent; too little value or
 any other failure reverts and leaves the delivery retriable. Morpho enforces position
 health.

@dev The soft gates shared by the borrow and the withdraw - the deposit carries no id and no
 deadline (see {ComposeReceiverAccountBase._terminalSkipReason}):
 a duplicate id or a stale deadline completes the delivery without executing; the
 bridged FXRP stays for the fixed rails.
