documentation.text:
@dev The withdraw action's return leg: sends exactly `_amount` FXRP to this account's
 own Flare address (same address on every chain) with the redeem-home compose - a
 deadline, this block time plus `REDEEM_HOME_TTL`, and nothing else - so the Flare twin
 redeems at most this amount on arrival. Equal validated decimals allow
 `minAmountLD == amountLD`. `_options` carry the Flare-side gas and, optionally, the
 redemption's executor fee as compose value. Exactly the quoted fee is spent from
 `_value` and the excess is forwarded to the parent (the endpoint is no refund target).

typeDescriptions.typeString: function (uint256) view external returns (struct IMorphoLoanMarketsFacet.FeeTerms memory)

documentation.text:
@dev Prices the elapsed period at the SNAPSHOTTED terms - `owed = max(floor·P·T,
 I + spread·P·T)` with `I = max(0, D − P)`, so an external repayment or liquidation
 counts as zero interest and the delta never underflows - then re-baselines: principal
 to the live debt, clock to now, snapshot to the current terms. The re-baseline runs
 on EVERY checkpoint (a first borrow must accrue at current terms, not stale ones).
 Shares-first: zero principal makes no Morpho call; a zero elapsed period skips the
 fee math but still re-reads the debt raw (a same-block checkpoint after an external
 repayment must not keep a stale base); zero live shares settle at `D = 0` without
 touching the IRM.

@dev The cover gate, shared by the withdraw (on the remainder after `_collateralOut`) and
 the borrow (on the post-borrow position, `_collateralOut == 0`): the collateral left in
 the position, valued at the market oracle's price, must cover {LoanMath.requiredCover} of
 the live debt and the collectible fee - Morpho's liquidation line with a fixed headroom, so
 the gate implies Morpho's health check and a fresh loan is gated at `EXIT_HEADROOM / LLTV`
 of its debt. The debt read here is accrued: the caller's checkpoint, or the borrow just
 made, brought it forward. With nothing owed the gate reads no oracle (and forgives
 debt-free dust); a zero, dead or reverting oracle values the remainder at nothing, so
 the action is refused - a withdrawal is then settled through repay, oracle-free, and
 retried, while a borrow needs the oracle back (Morpho, whose check ran first inside the
 borrow, reads it too). Reverts `InsufficientRemainingCollateral` with the two numbers.

@dev A sub-unit remainder on a debt-free position can never be transferred (ERC-20
 moves whole units) and never grows again - a raw-zero gate would park the exit
 forever over dust, so it is forgiven when a gate passes with nothing collectible.
 Reached only then, so the remainder is sub-unit by construction; a whole unit or more
 is a collectible fee and is never forgiven.

@dev The tail of {repay}, over the balance a closed or debt-free position leaves: pay
 `min(collectible, balance)` to the fee recipient ({_payFee}, best-effort, never rolling
 back the repayment), then reserve as much of the still-outstanding fee as the remaining
 balance covers (a later repay retries that reservation without a new top-up; an
 uncovered shortfall needs new funds) and send only the unreserved balance to the
 parent, once debt-free.

@dev Pays `_amount` (non-zero) of the collectible fee from this account's balance to
 the fee recipient, best-effort: nothing moves when the token refuses the recipient
 (RLUSD can freeze addresses), so a repayment never rolls back; the fee debt shrinks
 only by the successfully requested transfer (conventional ERC-20 semantics are a
 registration policy). Not held by the pause: the money goes to Flare's own recipient,
 where an overcharge would be refundable, and holding it only made the paused route
 debt-first. Returns the amount paid - zero when nothing moved.

documentation.text:
@dev The type's governance-set fee recipient. Debt, or a collectible fee, implies it
 is configured: the terms are the borrow activation marker.

typeDescriptions.typeString: function (uint256) view external returns (struct IMorphoLoanMarketsFacet.Market memory)

documentation.text:
@dev The account's one market, bound write-once to its type. If its Morpho stops
 answering, this account's debt-gated paths block - inherent to where the position
 lives; hence the operational policy of only canonical immutable Morpho Blue deployments
 of the pinned v1.0.0 implementation (any other needs the conformance verification repeated).
@dev The account's collateral on its market, a plain Morpho storage read.

@dev The account's live borrow shares on its market - the exact test for "is there
 any debt", read live from Morpho every time (nothing is cached).

@dev The pause rule shared by the two collateral deposits: defending an indebted position
 survives a pause, like repayment, while a debt-free deposit is new exposure and waits it
 out. Debt increases and withdrawals never route through here - they stop outright. The
 pause is read first, on every deposit: unpaused - the common case - that is one
 controller read and no position read, and a controller that cannot answer the pause
 question refuses every deposit, indebted or not, the same fail-closed posture as
 {_checkNotPaused}.

@dev The market oracle's price, zero when the oracle is dead, reverting or answers zero -
 the gate's own treatment, so a quote reads the collateral the way the gate will.

typeDescriptions.typeString: function (struct IMorpho.MarketParams memory,struct IMorpho.Market memory) view external returns (uint256)

documentation.text:
@dev The market brought forward to this block the way Morpho's own accrual will bring it -
 the rate model's view rate compounded over the time since the market's last update, added
 to the borrow and supply totals within their uint128 bounds (a market without a rate model
 earns nothing) - and this account's shares, collateral and the debt those shares represent
 on the accrued totals. Reverts where the rate model does: every debt-bearing action would.

@dev The lowest oracle price at which Morpho's health check still passes: its value floors
 twice (the collateral's value, then that value at the LLTV), so the price is the smallest
 that keeps the floored value at or above `ceil(debt / LLTV)`. Zero when debt-free; the
 maximum value with debt and no collateral.

@dev The largest further borrow the cover passes against `_value` of collateral. The
 closed form - the claim the value covers, less the debt and the fee's weight - ignores
 Morpho's share rounding on the way in and out, so the exact bound is found by bisection on
 the post-borrow debt as {_borrowTo} will see it: zero passes (the position is
 covered, or the closed form would be zero) and two past the closed form fails (one beyond
 what a share of rounding can add; were it ever to pass, the result would be a passing,
 non-maximal amount, never an unsafe one).

@dev The debt after borrowing `_more` on the accrued market: Morpho rounds the new shares
 up on the way in and the debt up on the way out.

@dev {repay}'s allocation of `_payment`, assuming every fee transfer succeeds: with live
 shares, the pro-rata fee share first when the payment is short of debt plus fee, then the
 debt (closed by shares when the rest covers it, otherwise repaid by assets with Morpho's
 rounding), then the tail - the collectible from what is left, a reservation for the rest,
 the surplus to the parent only once debt-free.

@dev The smallest top-up whose {repay} (with `_idle` already on the account) leaves a
 position the cover passes at `_valueLeft`: a binary search over the top-up, since
 every unit paid shrinks both claims; closing both claims (debt plus collectible less the
 idle balance) always suffices, so the search is bounded.

documentation.text:
@dev Whether the position {_simulateRepay} leaves after `_payment` is covered by
 `_valueLeft`.

@dev The value, in loan tokens, of the collateral left after `_collateralOut` at `_price`,
 rounded down; nothing when nothing is left.

@title MorphoLoanSubaccountRemote contract
 @notice The loan-chain-side subaccount implementation (Ethereum, at launch): same frozen
 proxy and CREATE2 address as the Flare-side account, resolved per type through the
 controller-as-beacon. Authenticated compose actions ({ComposeReceiverAccountBase}), sent by
 this same account on Flare, operate on its type's write-once Morpho market - so the address
 itself commits to the pool. Repayment, idle-collateral deposit and the fee checkpoint are
 permissionless fixed rails, and nothing here is parent-callable: Morpho collateral and debt
 move only behind the compose authentication. Idle FXRP has
 one route, into the position ({depositIdleFxrp}), from where the signed withdraw action
 brings it home under the position's ordinary conditions. Across the rails and the signed
 actions every destination is fixed on-chain - the account's own position, the parent, the
 governance-set fee recipient, or (the withdraw's return leg) this account's own address on
 Flare - so no caller ever

 the canonical `morpho-org/morpho-blue` `IIrm` v1.0.0. `borrowRateView` is what the account's
 read surface uses to bring a market's debt forward to the current block the way Morpho's own
 accrual will; `borrowRate` is the state-changing twin Morpho calls when it accrues. Kept as our
 own MIT code because the upstream files are GPL-2.0-or-later; conformance is pinned by
 `test/unit/smartAccounts/MorphoConformance.t.sol`.

@dev WAD fixed point: the fee rates' and the headroom's precision.
@dev The fee's year: annual WAD rates accrue over a fixed 365-day year.

@dev The cover gate's headroom over Morpho's liquidation line (WAD): the collateral left
 after an action must be worth `EXIT_HEADROOM / LLTV` of the covered claim, where Morpho
 itself lets a position run down to `1 / LLTV` (its withdraw, borrow and liquidation tests
 are one and the same). At the launch market's 77% LLTV this is exactly 1.5x.

@dev The cover gate's required cover, in loan tokens: `(debt + FEE_WEIGHT * collectible)
 * EXIT_HEADROOM / lltv`, rounded up; zero when nothing is owed.

@dev The fee one elapsed period adds, at WAD precision (base units x 1e18):
 `max(P * floor * T / YEAR, I * WAD + P * spread * T / YEAR) - I * WAD` over the principal
 `P` at the period's start (base units), the WAD annual rates, the period's length `T` in
 seconds of the 365-day year, and the market interest `I = max(0, liveDebt - P)` the period
 produced in base units - an external repayment or a liquidation counts as zero interest,
 so the delta never underflows. Each rate term is one `mulDiv` rounded down, the interest
 exact. Zero for a zero principal or a zero period.

 collectible)` rounded down; the remainder goes to the debt.

@title MorphoMath
 @notice Our own MIT implementation of the pieces of Morpho Blue arithmetic the accounts
 depend on: the market id (`keccak256(abi.encode(marketParams))`, Morpho's `MarketParamsLib.id`),
 the share/asset conversions with Morpho's virtual offsets (`SharesMathLib`: one virtual
 asset, 1e6 virtual shares, rounding as named) and the interest compounding of its accrual
 (`MathLib.wTaylorCompounded`, the third-order Taylor polynomial of `e^(rate * elapsed) - 1`
 that `_accrueInterest` applies to the borrow total). Written here rather than imported because the
 upstream libraries are GPL-2.0-or-later; equality with `morpho-blue` v1.0.0 (commit 55d2d99)
 is pinned by `test/unit/smartAccounts/MorphoConformance.t.sol` on fixed vectors. The full-precision `mulDiv`
 agrees with Morpho's checked multiplication everywhere Morpho itself does not revert.

 accounts: the loan-chain subaccount and Personal Account (Ethereum, at launch), and the Flare
 loan subaccount as the receiver of its own bridge-back. It authenticates the endpoint, the
 OFT, the origin chain, the pinned peer and `composeFrom`, and tracks replay state for the
 signed actions (an id-less action, such as the Flare redeem-home - which itself originates
 from a signed withdraw - carries no id and relies on the endpoint's at-most-once
 compose delivery). Users are XRPL-only and their
 signatures become on-chain authority only on Flare, so every action arriving here was sent by
 this same address on the other chain — the account's own twin. Account-specific
 parent-driven and public rails live outside this interface.

 operator quotes the return leg first, puts that fee (plus headroom; the excess lands on

 message.

@notice Reverts on a loan instruction whose arguments cannot execute on the loan chain:
 a zero operation id or a deadline already passed (borrow and withdraw), a zero borrow,
 deposit or withdrawal amount, a borrow disbursement that is not a clean non-zero EVM address other than
 this account, a borrow naming a delivery-value floor for a destination kind that cannot
 spend value, or a withdraw with a zero delivery-value floor. Checked here, before any
 bridge fee is paid.

@notice The borrow instruction: bridges `_collateralAmount` FXRP (zero for a borrow
 against existing collateral) with the typed payload that supplies it as collateral,
 borrows `_borrowAmount` on the loan-chain twin's market and disburses it. A pure
 collateral deposit is its own instruction, {depositCollateral}.
 @dev Restricted to the parent Personal Account: the instruction names a loan action and
 a user-chosen disbursement destination, so it must carry the user's XRPL signature. The
 payload is built here, not passed in, so a malformed payload cannot reach the bridge; the
 envelope and the EVM destination are validated before quoting
 ({InvalidLoanInstruction}) and the loan chain re-validates on delivery. It sends to this
 account's own cross-chain address through the configured pinned peer, sharing the
 bridging core's guards: paused reverts, a configured route that is not suspended required,
 live peer re-checked. `_extraOptions` must be type-3 options carrying both the destination
 `lzReceive` gas and the `lzCompose` gas. `msg.value` must cover the LayerZero fee; the
 excess is refunded to the parent. On the loan chain the borrow is also refused, retriably,
 when the post-borrow position would fall under the cover gate
 (`InsufficientRemainingCollateral`) - the same rule that gates {withdraw}: the collateral
 must be worth `1.155 / LLTV` of the debt plus twice the collectible Flare fee.
 @param _collateralAmount FXRP to bridge and supply as collateral; may be zero, at most
 the account's balance.
 @param _borrowAmount Loan-token amount to borrow and disburse; non-zero.
 @param _destinationKind The disbursement destination kind (`DESTINATION_KIND_*`).
 @param _destination The disbursement destination (a clean zero-padded EVM address for
 `DESTINATION_KIND_EVM`).
 @param _minComposeValue The delivery-value floor for a destination kind that spends
 compose value on the loan chain, in the loan chain's native token. Reserved: every kind V1
 supports disburses without spending value, so `DESTINATION_KIND_EVM` requires zero and a
 non-zero floor is refused here, before any bridge fee. It exists in the frozen V1 payload
 to reduce what enabling a kind that does pay for its own onward delivery has to move -
 implementations and governed parameters rather than the wire schema. It does not
 guarantee that: a floor protects delivery funding and settles nothing about quote
 validity, a spending cap, or an XRPL destination tag, so a kind needing any of those
 still arrives as a new payload version. Its meaning, once such a kind
 exists, is the withdraw's: the loan chain refuses any delivery of this borrow - execution
 and terminal skip alike - carrying less than this, so a front-run with less cannot consume
 the packet and burn the prepaid value.
 @param _operationId The user-chosen operation id (non-zero, unique per subaccount).
 @param _deadline Unix time after which the loan chain skips the instruction unexecuted.
 Keep it short (under an hour): the loan is priced at the type's fee terms current at
 delivery, so the front end warns while a terms change is pending in the timelock, and a
 short deadline is what bounds how far past that warning a delayed packet can execute.
 @param _extraOptions Caller-supplied LayerZero execution options (type-3).

@notice The cancel instruction: a message-only send that consumes `_operationId` on the
 loan chain, so a borrow or withdraw packet carrying that id can never execute.
 @dev Restricted to the parent Personal Account. The motivating case is a borrow parked by
 a failed health check after a price drop, which any collateral landing - the user's own
 deposit or the permissionless rail - would otherwise make executable again. Sending this
 is not cancellation: the two packets race, an original that lands first executes
 normally and the cancellation then finalizes silently - so a client resolves a sent
 cancellation by whichever arrives, the loan chain's
 {IMorphoLoanSubaccountRemote.LoanActionCancelled} or the original action's own execution event,
 either of which ends the instruction's live state; and an id a cancellation was signed
 for is retired for good. It carries no deadline (a late
 cancellation is unnecessary or still correct). On the loan chain it is not pause-gated;
 here it travels the ordinary instruction path, which a Flare pause closes like every
 other instruction (the controller's instruction facets and the bridge send both check
 it), so a parked packet cannot be revoked from a paused Flare. In that state the loan
 chain's own pause suspends the borrow but cancels nothing, so the order is: pause the loan
 chain, restore Flare when safe, submit and confirm the cancellation while the loan chain
 stays paused, then resume - unpausing it earlier makes the latent packet executable again.
 Burning an unissued id is allowed and makes a re-send harmless.
 @param _operationId The operation id to consume; must be non-zero.
 @param _extraOptions LayerZero options for the cancel message (gas only - it moves no
 tokens and needs no compose value).

 the condition is temporary-by-policy and a permissionless delivery must not consume
 the packet.

 spends no compose value on this chain. Every kind V1 supports disburses without spending

 that pays for its own onward delivery. The Flare sender refuses the same instruction
 before any bridge fee is paid.

@notice Repays the account's debt and the accrued Flare fee with its idle loan-token
 balance: a payment short of the two is split pro rata between them, a covering one
 closes the debt, attempts the whole collectible (reserving anything unpaid) and returns
 the surplus to the parent.
 @dev Permissionless and pause-exempt throughout: the debt reduction only moves the
 account's own position toward safety, and the fee legs only move money to Flare's own
 recipient. It checkpoints before the repayment and re-syncs
 the canonical debt after (see {checkpointFee}). With live debt `D` and collectible fee
 `F`, interest accrues, then a balance `P < D + F` pays `P × F / (D + F)` (rounded down)
 to the fee recipient first and repays Morpho with the rest - by exact borrow shares when
 that rest covers the debt (no over-repay revert), otherwise by assets; a balance covering
 `D + F` closes the debt by exact shares and attempts the whole collectible from the
 remainder. Every fee payment is best-effort, never held by the pause (an overcharge
 would land on Flare's own recipient and is refundable), never rolling back the
 repayment ({LoanFeeCollected}; the fee debt shrinks only by the
 successfully requested transfer, conventional ERC-20 semantics being a
 market-registration policy): a share that cannot be paid stays in the balance and
 repays debt ({LoanFeeDeferred}), and once debt-free the remainder is attempted again,
 with as much of it as the outstanding fee needs reserved here ({LoanFeeReserved}). Only
 the unreserved balance is pushed to the parent once debt-free ({LoanSurplusRecovered};
 best-effort, {LoanSurplusRetained} on refusal). Settling both claims through this rail
 therefore costs the live debt plus the collectible fee, from one balance in one call; a
 payment that covers the debt but not the fee leaves a pro-rata sliver of both, unless
 the debt closes for less: a paid share's round-down can leave exactly the debt (possible
 within roughly `F / D` base units of `D + F`), and a deferred share leaves the full
 payment available, which may cover it - Morpho then consumes exactly the debt and the
 tail handles any remainder, with fee still outstanding. The default route pays the fee
 alongside the debt; repaying Morpho directly, on this account's behalf, pays the debt
 alone.
 @return _assets The assets repaid.

@notice Runs a bare fee checkpoint: prices the elapsed period at the snapshotted
 terms, adds the result to the fee debt, and re-baselines (principal to the canonical
 live debt, clock to now, snapshot to the current terms).
 @dev Permissionless and pause-exempt - notably the liquidated account's relief: an
 external repayment or liquidation is invisible to the account, so the floor keeps
 accruing on the stale principal until someone checkpoints, and only prospectively.
 Under unchanged terms and non-decreasing debt, splitting a period typically increases
 the total fee and never decreases it by more than one X18 unit (under 1e-18 of a base
 unit) per checkpoint, so checkpointing cannot be used against the protocol; the
 advertised promise is that per-checkpoint measurement. Shares-first: zero principal
 makes no Morpho call, zero live shares settle at zero debt without touching the IRM.

@title IMorphoLoanSubaccountRemote
 @notice User interface for the loan-chain-side subaccount (Ethereum, at launch), at the same
 CREATE2 address as its Flare counterpart. Authenticated compose payloads, sent by this same
 account on Flare, execute the typed actions on the type's write-once Morpho market — so the
 address itself commits to the pool. Repayment, idle-collateral deposit and the fee
 checkpoint are permissionless fixed rails, and nothing here is parent-callable. Idle FXRP
 has one route, into the position ({depositIdleFxrp}), from where
 the signed withdraw action brings it home under the position's ordinary conditions. Across
 the rails and the signed actions every destination is fixed on-chain - the account's own
 position, the parent, the governance-set fee recipient, or (the withdraw's return leg) this
 account's own address on Flare - while the one user-chosen destination is a signed
 borrow's disbursement. It has no native rail.

 recorded redeemer, so every outcome - a partial fill, a payment-default payout, a refund
 - lands here, where {executeUserOp} handles anything, including triggering the default on

@title IPersonalAccountRemote
 @notice User interface for the remote Personal Account: the implementation
 registered behind the frozen PA proxy on a diamond other than Flare's (the loan chain,
 Ethereum, at launch),
 living at the same CREATE2 address as the user's Flare Personal Account. It has no local
 owner and no controller-driven methods — instructions exist only on Flare — so every
 authorized action arrives as an authenticated LayerZero compose message sent by this same
 account on Flare (`sendCrossChainUserOp`). The action set is exactly one action: execute
 a signed batch of calls, the way the Flare account executes `executeUserOp`. The blast
 radius is therefore the same as a controller compromise on Flare: a compromised compose
 root has the full on-chain authority of this address - balances, approvals, external
 positions and any role granted to it - and over the loan subaccount no direct authority at
 all: it has no parent-callable method, so Morpho collateral and debt stay behind the
 subaccount's own compose authentication. There is
 no permissionless rail: what arrives here (borrow proceeds the user directed here,
 recovered loan-token surplus, strays, native delivered with a message to fund
 value-carrying calls) moves only by the user's signature.

@title IBridgeRoutesFacet
 @notice Interface for the BridgeRoutesFacet contract: the Flare-side, governance-set routing
 for everything that bridges FXRP or sends a compose message from an account here to that same
 account's address on a remote chain — the subaccounts of every type and the Personal Account's
 cross-chain user operations. Three records: the one FXRP OFT adapter on Flare, one pinned peer
 per remote chain (a route), and the remote chain each subaccount type lives on. The Flare
 counterpart of the remote diamonds' {IComposeTransportFacet}: a transport says how composes
 arrive on a remote, a route says where sends go from here. Cut only on the Flare diamond.
 @dev Routes are governance-set rather than supplied by the caller, so that no caller can choose
 where assets are bridged: a subaccount's destination is the route of its type, and a Personal
 Account's cross-chain user operation names a destination endpoint that must be a registered
 route. Every send also re-checks the OFT's live peer for the destination against the pinned one,
 so a peer mutation on the adapter after configuration fails the sends closed instead of routing
 to an unknown remote OApp.

 OFT is wired to.

 zero-padded EVM address), or does not match the OFT's live peer for the origin endpoint.

@title IComposeTransportFacet
 @notice The compose transport of a remote diamond: one record per diamond naming the
 LayerZero endpoint that may call `lzCompose`, the OFT that must be the compose sender, the
 origin chain and the pinned peer there. Every compose receiver on the diamond — the remote
 Personal Account and every remote subaccount type — authenticates against it, so it is the
 security root of every action that arrives without a local signature. One route per
 diamond: a token bridged through a different OFT would need a transport per route, which is
 a schema change, not a setting. Cut only on remote diamonds (the loan chain, Ethereum, at
 launch).
 @dev The transport is written under the timelock and cleared immediately: the clear is the
 containment lever for a compromised endpoint, OFT or peer, and a lever behind a timelock is
 not one. The clear does not cancel queued `setComposeTransport` calls (the timelock keys them
 by calldata hash and lets anyone execute a matured one - cancel them first), and it does not
 retire compose packets already queued at the endpoint (a delivery that reverts against a
 cleared transport stays retriable). The incident runbook is therefore: pause, cancel queued
 transport sets, clear, and later set a replacement transport that rotates the compromised
 identity - the exact compromised tuple is never restored, or packets forged under it would
 pass authentication again.

@title IMorphoLoanMarketsFacet
 @notice Governance-set per-type configuration of the remote loan subaccounts: a write-once

 pool — and mutable Flare fee terms. Registration pins the collateral token to the transport
 OFT's token, for that market and every later transport; the first non-zero fee recipient
 activates borrowing. Cut only on the loan-chain diamond (Ethereum, at launch).

@dev Calculate the modular multiplicative inverse of a number in Z/nZ.
 If n is a prime, then Z/nZ is a field. In that case all elements are inversible, except 0.
 If n is not a prime, then Z/nZ is not a field, and some elements might not be inversible.
 If the input value is not inversible, 0 is returned.
 NOTE: If you know for sure that n is (big) a prime, it may be cheaper to use Fermat's little theorem and get the
 inverse using `Math.modExp(a, n - 2, n)`. See {invModPrime}.

@dev Variant of {invMod}. More efficient, but only works if `p` is known to be a prime greater than `2`.
 From https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fermat%27s_little_theorem[Fermat's little theorem], we know that if p is
 prime, then `a**(p-1) ≡ 1 mod p`. As a consequence, we have `a * a**(p-2) ≡ 1 mod p`, which means that
 `a**(p-2)` is the modular multiplicative inverse of a in Fp.
 NOTE: this function does NOT check that `p` is a prime greater than `2`.

@dev Wrappers over Solidity's uintXX/intXX/bool casting operators with added overflow
 checks.
 Downcasting from uint256/int256 in Solidity does not revert on overflow. This can
 easily result in undesired exploitation or bugs, since developers usually
 assume that overflows raise errors. `SafeCast` restores this intuition by
 reverting the transaction when such an operation overflows.
 Using this library instead of the unchecked operations eliminates an entire
 class of bugs, so it's recommended to use it always.

Prove that a block with given number and timestamp exists and
 update the current underlying block info if the provided data is higher.
 This method should be called by minters before minting and by agent's regularly
 to prevent current block being too outdated, which gives too short time for
 minting or redemption payment.
 NOTE: anybody can call.

Due to the minting pool fees or after a lot size change by the governance,
 it may happen that less than one lot remains on a redemption ticket. This is named "dust" and

 @author Flare
 @notice A detection of a transaction that either decreases the balance for some address or is
 signed by the source address.
 Such an attestation could prove a violation of an agreement and therefore provides grounds to liquidate
 some funds locked by a smart contract on Flare.
 A transaction is considered “balance decreasing” for the address, if the balance after the
 transaction is lower than before or the address is among the signers of the transaction

 @custom:verification The transaction with `transactionId` is fetched from the API of the
 source blockchain node or relevant indexer.
 If the transaction cannot be fetched or the transaction is in a block that does not have a
 sufficient number of confirmations, the attestation request is rejected.
 Once the transaction is received, the response fields are extracted if the transaction is balance
 decreasing for the indicated address.
 Some of the request and response fields are chain specific as described below.
 The fields can be computed with the help of a balance decreasing summary.
 ### UTXO (Bitcoin and Dogecoin)
 - `sourceAddressIndicator` is the the index of the transaction input in hex padded to a 0x prefixed 32-byte string.
 If the indicated input does not exist or the indicated input does not have the address,
 the attestation request is rejected.
 The `sourceAddress` is the address of the indicated transaction input.
 - `spentAmount` is the sum of values of all inputs with sourceAddress minus the sum of
 all outputs with `sourceAddress`.
 Can be negative.
 - `blockTimestamp` is the mediantime of a block.
 ### XRPL
 - `sourceAddressIndicator` is the standard address hash of the address whose balance has been decreased.
 If the address indicated by `sourceAddressIndicator` is not among the signers of the transaction and the balance
 of the address was not lowered in the transaction, the attestation request is rejected.
 - `spentAmount` is the difference between the balance of the indicated address after and before the transaction.
 Can be negative.
 - `blockTimestamp` is the close_time of a ledger converted to unix time.

 @author Flare
 @notice Assertion that an agreed-upon payment has not been made by a certain deadline.
 A confirmed request shows that a transaction meeting certain criteria (address, amount, reference)
 did not appear in the specified block range.
 This type of attestation can be used to e.g. provide grounds to liquidate funds locked by a smart
 contract on Flare when a payment is missed.
 @custom:verification If `firstOverflowBlock` cannot be determined or does not have a sufficient
 number of confirmations, the attestation request is rejected.
 If `firstOverflowBlockNumber` is higher or equal to `minimalBlockNumber`, the request is rejected.
 The search range are blocks between heights including `minimalBlockNumber` and excluding `firstOverflowBlockNumber`.
 If the verifier does not have a view of all blocks from `minimalBlockNumber` to `firstOverflowBlockNumber`,
 the attestation request is rejected.
 The request is confirmed if no transaction meeting the specified criteria is found in the search range.
 The criteria and timestamp are chain specific.
 ### UTXO (Bitcoin and Dogecoin)
 Criteria for the transaction:
 - It is not coinbase transaction.
 - The transaction has the specified standardPaymentReference.
 - The sum of values of all outputs with the specified address minus the sum of values of all inputs with
 the specified address is greater than `amount` (in practice the sum of all values of the inputs with the
 specified address is zero).
 Timestamp is `mediantime`.
 ### XRPL
 Criteria for the transaction:
 - The transaction is of type payment.
 - The transaction has the specified standardPaymentReference,
 - One of the following is true:
   - Transaction status is `SUCCESS` and the amount received by the specified destination address is
 greater than the specified `value`.
   - Transaction status is `RECEIVER_FAILURE` and the specified destination address would receive an
 amount greater than the specified `value` had the transaction been successful.
 Timestamp is `close_time` converted to UNIX time.
 @custom:lut `minimalBlockTimestamp`
 @custom:lutlimit `0x127500`, `0x127500`, `0x127500`

Finalization function for new signing policies and protocol messages.
 It can be used as finalization contract on Flare chain or as relay contract on other EVM chain.
 Can be called in two modes. It expects calldata that is parsed in a custom manner.
 Hence the transaction calls should assemble relevant calldata in the 'data' field.
 Depending on the data provided, the contract operations in essentially two modes:
 (1) Relaying signing policy. The structure of the calldata is:
        function signature (4 bytes) + active signing policy
             + 0 (1 byte) + new signing policy,
     total of exactly 4423 bytes.
 (2) Relaying signed message. The structure of the calldata is:
        function signature (4 bytes) + signing policy
           + signed message (38 bytes) + ECDSA signatures with indices (67 bytes each)
     This case splits into two subcases:
     - protocolMessageId = 1: Message id must be of the form (protocolMessageId, 0, 0, merkleRoot).
       The validity of the signatures of sufficient weight is checked and if
       successful, the merkleRoot from the message is returned (32 bytes) and the
       reward epoch id of the signing policy as well (additional 3 bytes)
     - protocolMessageId > 1: The validity of the signatures of sufficient weight is checked and if
       it is valid, the merkleRoot is published for protocolId and votingRoundId.
 Reverts if relaying is not successful.

 @author Flare
 @notice Assertion that an agreed-upon XRP payment has not been made by a certain deadline.
 A confirmed request shows that a transaction meeting certain criteria (address, amount, reference) did not appear
 in the specified block range.
 This type of attestation can be used to e.g. provide grounds to liquidate funds locked by a smart contract on
 Flare when a payment is missed.
 @custom:verification If `firstOverflowBlock` cannot be determined or does not have a sufficient
 [number of confirmations](/specs/attestations/configs.md#finalityconfirmation), the attestation
 request is rejected.
 If `firstOverflowBlockNumber` is higher or equal to `minimalBlockNumber`, the request is rejected.
 The search range are blocks between heights including `minimalBlockNumber` and excluding `firstOverflowBlockNumber`.
 If the verifier does not have a view of all blocks from `minimalBlockNumber` to `firstOverflowBlockNumber`,
  the attestation request is rejected.
 The request is confirmed if no transaction meeting the specified criteria is found in the search range.
 Criteria for the transaction:
 - The transaction is of type payment.
 - The destination address hash matches the hash of the destination address of the transaction.
 - If `checkFirstMemoData` is true, the hash of the MemoData field of the first Memo in the transaction matches
 `firstMemoDataHash`.
 - If `checkDestinationTag` is true, the destination tag of the transaction matches `destinationTag`.
 At least one of the fields `checkFirstMemoData` and `checkDestinationTag` must be true for the request to be valid.
 - One of the following is true:
   - Transaction status is `SUCCESS` and the amount received by the specified destination address is greater
  than the specified `value`.
   - Transaction status is `RECEIVER_FAILURE` and the specified destination address would receive an amount
 greater than the specified `value` had the transaction been successful.
 Timestamp is `close_time` converted to UNIX time.
 @custom:lut `minimalBlockTimestamp`
 @custom:lutlimit `0x127500`
